panelPlan.action: Insert: Astrid turns the unfamiliar metal handle at the sink and water suddenly runs. Her hand stops in place; this is a first encounter, not routine appliance use.
Medium: Astrid tests the stream with her fingers, then turns the handle off and on once more to confirm that her action controls it.
Low medium: Gunnar crouches beneath the sink and follows the visible metal pipes into the wall without touching fittings or pretending to know their purpose.
Two-shot Bjorn/Carrie: Bjorn looks from the flowing water to the wall and asks the question that matters in his world: where is the source and who is moving it.
Wide: Carrie cannot give them a satisfying mechanical explanation. Astrid keeps the water running while the others continue unpacking around this impossible convenience.

dialogueInline.text: It comes when I turn this.
And leaves through that hole.
Sink, drain, pipes. Those are the names. The rest takes longer.
Where is the well?
There isn't a well in the building.
Then why does water climb five floors when Astrid turns that metal?
I can't explain water pressure well enough to survive that question.
The metal under here is warm.
That one brings hot water.
There is hot water in the wall.

panelPlan.action: Wide: Carrie empties the DTI emergency grocery bag onto the table: crackers, protein bars, bottled water, disposable utensils.
Medium on Bjorn looking at the food, then at the five displaced adults.
Medium: Gunnar checks the bag itself as though more food may be hidden in a seam.
Medium at the rear window: Gunnar smells food from the street below; outside, pigeons are visible on the iron structure beyond the window, but nobody comments on them yet.
Wide: Carrie puts her coat back on and deliberately takes only Bjorn and Gunnar. Astrid and the two male Kin remain in the apartment with the unpacked gear and nearly empty food bag.

dialogueInline.text: Is this the food they sent with five people?
It was meant to get you through intake, not establish a winter hall.
Your department prepares for hunger by making it measurable.
My department assumed I'd get you somewhere with food.
Bread, onions. Something frying below.
Corner shop. Open all night.
We have silver.
Bring it. You and Gunnar are coming with me.
Astrid, I am not taking six people into one corner store.
We'll stay.

panelPlan.action: Wide: Carrie enters the compact bodega with Bjorn and Gunnar only. Ordinary customers continue shopping. The owner looks up once and goes back to work.

Medium: Carrie chooses basic groceries quickly. Bjorn judges recognizable food by sight; Gunnar compares objects, quantities and containers physically, turning packages in his hands and smelling produce.
Counter close: Bjorn sets a small piece of hacksilver beside the groceries. The owner examines the offered metal and calmly refuses it.
Medium at the payment terminal: Carrie taps her modern card while the owner waits and Bjorn and Gunnar study the unfamiliar exchange.
Medium: Bjorn watches the owner bag the food and watches Carrie's transaction complete; his concern is that Carrie has somehow paid, not how the mechanism works.
Close: the owner slides the hacksilver back to Bjorn.

dialogueInline.text: For the food.
Sorry. Can't take silver.
Good silver.
I'll pay.
You touched two black things. Where is the money?
We're doing money on a different day.
How much?
Fifty-eight dollars and forty cents.
Then I owe you that.
You can owe me dinner by not starting a monetary theory before we eat it.
Take your silver.
You refuse good metal very calmly.
I get all kinds.

panelPlan.action: Wide from inside 5B: the door opens and Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar return carrying grocery bags. Astrid and First Male Kin are arranging bedding and the room. Second Male Kin is at the rear window beside a bowl containing one very alive pigeon.
Medium: Carrie stops with the grocery bags still in her hands. Bjorn looks from the bags to the bird. Gunnar immediately notices the cord running out through the open window.
Medium on Second Male Kin: he explains the obvious logic—there were birds outside and the household needed food.
Two-shot Bjorn/Second Male Kin: Bjorn regards the successful catch as competent work, while Carrie is already walking toward the window to inspect where it happened.
Close on Carrie looking through the window and seeing that the cord has been rigged across part of the exterior iron landing toward the neighboring section.

dialogueInline.text: Why is there a pigeon in a bowl?
For dinner.
We brought dinner.
Now there is more.
Did you catch it here?
Birds sit on the iron outside. I had cord.
Did you make a snare on that?
It worked.
Nobody touch the pigeon for one minute.
It has already been touched.
Then nobody improve the situation while I look at it.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio main window and fire escape
panelPlan.action: Wide at the rear window: Carrie leans out just enough to inspect the exterior iron landing. Second Male Kin shows where he tied the snare. Gunnar studies the iron stairs physically from inside the window.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio main window and fire escape
panelPlan.action: Medium: Carrie points down the connected iron flights and explains that people use them to escape if the interior stair cannot be used.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio main window and fire escape
panelPlan.action: Medium on Bjorn looking down the route to the ground, immediately understanding it as a second road out of the room.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio main window and fire escape
panelPlan.action: Medium on Second Male Kin: he looks at the cord crossing part of that route and concedes the placement problem, not the hunting premise.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio main window and fire escape
panelPlan.action: Wide: Second Male Kin frees the pigeon and removes the cord from their section. Unknown to them, a separate loose end remains beyond the neighboring window.

dialogueInline.text: This ironwork is for getting people out if the stairs inside cannot be used.
The city calls it a fire escape.
Then it is a second road from the room.
A narrow one.
An exit has to stay clear. Immediately.
Then the snare was badly placed.
Yes. And there are no snares on the fire escape.
Those are two judgments.
I am making both.
The bird is still food.
The bird is leaving.

panelPlan.location: Fifth-floor hallway outside apartment 5B, before the first meal
panelPlan.action: Wide: knock at 5B. Upstairs Neighbor stands in the hall holding a separate length of cord she removed from beside her window. Carrie opens the door; Second Male Kin is visible behind her and recognizes it immediately.

panelPlan.location: Fifth-floor hallway outside apartment 5B, before the first meal
panelPlan.action: Medium: Neighbor holds the cord out. Second Male Kin explains where he tied it, revealing that his idea of the household boundary extended too far.

panelPlan.location: Fifth-floor hallway outside apartment 5B, before the first meal
panelPlan.action: Medium: Carrie gives a direct apology. Astrid appears with one unopened spicy packaged snack from the bodega bag.

panelPlan.location: Fifth-floor hallway outside apartment 5B, before the first meal
panelPlan.action: Close: Astrid offers the snack; Neighbor takes it after a beat without becoming friendly.

panelPlan.location: Fifth-floor hallway outside apartment 5B, before the first meal
panelPlan.action: Wide: Neighbor walks away with the problem settled only provisionally. Carrie closes the door while Second Male Kin looks at the now-returned cord in his hand.

dialogueInline.text: This was tied next to my window.
I tied it beside ours.
It crossed mine.
The part outside my window is mine enough.
It's down now, and it stays down. I'm sorry.
For trouble.
What is it?
Spicy.
The bird was released.
Was there a bird?
Briefly.
Keep it that way.

panelPlan.action: Wide: Astrid examines the unfamiliar stove while Carrie demonstrates one control once. Second Male Kin is visibly empty-handed after losing the pigeon; the grocery bags are now open on the counter.
Medium: flame or burner heat appears from the stove. Astrid immediately understands the practical result even though the mechanism is alien.
Wide: cooking begins. A little smoke rises higher than expected.
Large reaction panel: the smoke alarm suddenly SHRIEKS. Bjorn and Gunnar react physically to an unexplained alarm while Carrie grabs a towel and clears smoke beneath it.

The alarm is quiet and the burner is low. Astrid finishes serving the food; the six adults eat around the cramped table and kitchenette. Bjorn and Gunnar look up once more at the ceiling device while Carrie sets the towel aside.

dialogueInline.text: Turn this. The fire comes from here.
Without wood.
Without wood.
BEEP! BEEP! BEEP! BEEP!
dialogueInline.speaker: SFX

dialogueInline.text: Don't hit the ceiling. It senses smoke and warns us.
We can see the smoke.
So it senses smoke but doesn't know what smoke is?
You have found the philosophical weakness of the smoke alarm.
The pigeon would have smoked less.
The pigeon is gone.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio table / phone on speaker
panelPlan.action: Medium at the table: Bjorn asks what can actually end a temporary placement.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio table / phone on speaker
panelPlan.action: Two-shot: Carrie answers from professional knowledge, distinguishing ordinary confusion from actual safety, damage, or conduct problems.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio table / phone on speaker
panelPlan.action: Reaction panel: Second Male Kin looks toward the returned snare cord beside his gear.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio table / phone on speaker
panelPlan.action: Medium: Carrie follows his eyeline and names the relevant problem without turning it into a lecture.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio table / phone on speaker
panelPlan.action: Close on Bjorn: the useful fact he takes away is that removal requires an actual reason, not that he has mastered housing law.

dialogueInline.text: You keep calling the room temporary. What ends it?
Review can change the placement. So can serious damage, violence, blocked exits, repeated safety problems or refusing essential terms.
Not knowing what the water in the wall is.
DTI would have no clients left if confusion were disqualifying.
The cord was on one of the ways out.
That's why I cared about the cord more than the pigeon.
It was removed.
Which is why you're still here instead of explaining it to Housing.
Then they need a reason to take the room.
A real one.

panelPlan.action: Wide: while the room inspection continues, First Male Kin drapes a damp wool garment over an exposed ceiling pipe because it is high and out of the way.
Fast medium: Carrie removes the garment immediately, careful not to strike the small sprinkler head.
Close: Carrie points only to the small metal head beside the pipe; no diagram or system explanation.
Reaction: First Male Kin studies the tiny object because the scale of the danger is not obvious.
Wide: the garment goes over a chair instead. Bjorn gestures toward Carrie's phone, trying to add the ceiling hazard to the condition record.

dialogueInline.text: Not there.
Why?
Break that little metal piece and a great deal of water comes out.
From the ceiling.
Enough that I do not want to demonstrate it.
Then record that too.
It's not damaged. Just don't hang anything on it.
Danger above the bedding is worth a record.
The wool has a chair now.

panelPlan.action: Insert: Carrie starts writing emergency numbers on a card, then stops after looking at the household.
Medium: she holds up her phone briefly; nobody mistakes it for something they know how to operate.
Medium: Carrie points toward the hallway and then downward, reducing the emergency plan to known people and known routes.
Two-shot Bjorn/Carrie: Bjorn accepts the human chain because it is concrete.
Wide at the doorway: Carrie finally reaches the point where she can leave.

dialogueInline.text: This card is useless to you tonight.
The marks are yours.
And none of you knows what to do with this.
You speak into it.
That is not enough to summon an ambulance.
Fire means leave. For injury or anything you can't handle, find the neighbor or the shopkeeper. Ask them to call for help.
The merchant and the neighbor.
Two people who know this city and already know where you live.
Better than the black glass.
For tonight.
